_note: Playoff series model and Cup simulation. Fitted on 165 playoff series 2013-14..2024-25 (excl. 2019-20 bubble). v1.3.0: P(A wins series) = average of two models that predicted past series about equally well once the choice itself was tested fairly: (1) every elite skater counted, (2) only the first two counted. Each: logistic(alpha * (b_power * power-rating gap + b_elite * elite gap)). Leave-one-season-out log-loss: power only 0.6624, every elite 0.6595, first two 0.6468, average 0.6509; with the threshold and count chosen fairly (nested) 0.6613. They disagree most for teams with 0 elite skaters (14 past series), where the evidence is thinnest, so the average is used. Elite = top-12 F and top-6 D by ice time with talent >= 90th percentile at the position. alpha 0.7 from the full Cup backtest (both models tied there).

series_backtest.note: Leave-one-season-out over 165 series. prob_score = % improvement in log-loss over a coin flip.

stage_skill.note: Backtest of the full simulation from about 4 and 14 games played, 8 seasons: improvement in log-loss over giving every team equal odds (alpha 0.7, elite counted up to 2).

cup_winners.note: Every Cup winner 2013-14..2024-25 (excl. 2019-20) had at least 2 elite (top-10%) skaters; 7 of 11 had 0 or 1 superstar (top 2%).

favorites: Each season's model favorite (avg ~13% Cup) won 0 of 8 Cups in the backtest (about 1 expected), so treat Cup odds as low-confidence.
